Adversarially verify this code-review finding from the M12 diff. Read the actual code (git diff main...HEAD + the file) and try to REFUTE it. Default to isReal=false if it's a false positive, pre-existing, out of scope, or already handled.

Lens: a11y
Severity: medium
File: components/customer/UpcomingBookings.tsx (saveReschedule(), line 55: announce(t("account.nextSession")))
Title: Reschedule success announces a meaningless label fragment to screen readers
Detail: After a successful reschedule the live region announces t("account.nextSession") which resolves to the bare string "Next session" (messages/en.json:362) — a UI label, not a confirmation of what just happened. The reschedule panel also closes (setRescheduleId(null)) and the inputs clear with no visible/announced success state, so a screen-reader user gets no meaningful feedback that the reschedule succeeded. Compare the cancel path on the same component (lines 35-38) which correctly announces a dedicated confirmation message. This is a live-region/feedback gap introduced by this diff.
Suggestion: Add a dedicated message (e.g. account.rescheduled = "Booking moved to your new time.") to messages/en.json and announce that instead of t("account.nextSession"). Consider surfacing it via toast(..., "success") for parity with the name-save flow, and move focus back to the booking's action area after the panel closes.

content.text:
All claims in the finding are verified. I have enough to conclude.

Verification summary:

1. **`account.nextSession` resolves to "Next session"** — Confirmed at `messages/en.json:362`: `"nextSession": "Next session"`. It's a bare UI label, not a confirmation of the reschedule action.

2. **It IS used elsewhere as a UI label heading** — `app/(customer)/account/page.tsx:121` uses `t("account.nextSession")` as a prefix label: `` `${t("account.nextSession")}: ${next.providerName} · ${next.whenLabel}` ``. This confirms it is a label fragment, not action feedback.

3. **The cancel path on the same component announces a dedicated confirmation** — Lines 35-38 announce `t("account.cancelledRefund")` ("Cancelled — your hold was released.") or `t("account.cancelledCharged")`. So there's a clear in-component precedent the reschedule path fails to match.

4. **The reschedule panel closes and inputs clear with no meaningful feedback** — Lines 53-55 do `setRescheduleId(null)`, `setNewTime("")`, then `announce(t("account.nextSession"))`. The success branch has no toast (unlike the error branches which `toast(..., "alert")`).

5. **The name-save flow uses `toast(..., "success")` for parity** — `NameSettingForm.tsx:25`: `toast(t("account.nameSaved"), "success")`, supporting the suggestion.

6. **Introduced by this diff** — The file is brand new in M12 (`new file mode 100644`).

7. **No dedicated `account.rescheduled` message exists yet** — grep confirms only `reschedule`, `rescheduleHeading`, `rescheduleSave` exist; no success-confirmation string.

I could find no grounds to refute. The announcement of `t("account.nextSession")` ("Next session") to the live region after a successful reschedule conveys no confirmation that the reschedule succeeded — a real a11y feedback gap, accurately scoped to medium severity, introduced by this diff.

In saveReschedule() (line 55) the success path announces t("account.nextSession") to the live region. That key resolves to the bare UI label "Next session" (messages/en.json:362) — and is in fact used elsewhere purely as a heading label (app/(customer)/account/page.tsx:121: `${t("account.nextSession")}: ...`), confirming it is a label fragment, not a confirmation of the action just performed. On success the panel also closes (setRescheduleId(null)) and clears the input (setNewTime("")) with no toast and no meaningful announced/visible success message, so a screen-reader user gets no confirmation the reschedule worked. The cancel path on the same component (lines 35-38) correctly announces a dedicated confirmation (account.cancelledRefund / account.cancelledCharged), and the name-save flow (NameSettingForm.tsx:25) uses toast(t("account.nameSaved"), "success"), so the suggested remedies have direct in-repo precedent. No dedicated account.rescheduled message currently exists (grep shows only reschedule/rescheduleHeading/rescheduleSave). The finding is accurate, in-scope, introduced by this diff, and not pre-existing or already handled. Medium severity is appropriate: meaningful work succeeds but the only feedback is a misleading/empty label fragment for assistive-tech users, an a11y feedback gap under WCAG/the project's a11y golden rule.
